segments.speaker: Rep
segments.text: Yeah, thanks for making the time, Dana. Quick apology on the slow follow-up from Monday. I lost almost the whole afternoon typing call notes into the CRM, fixing duplicate account records, and pulling together the deal desk packet, and it honestly crowded out the time I should have spent talking with you and the other buyers. So, not ideal. I did get the revised quote ready for 38 seats.

segments.speaker: Customer
segments.text: Okay, appreciate it. The 38 seats is right for the first phase. We may add 12 more in November, but finance only approved the initial group for now.

segments.speaker: Rep
segments.text: Got it. For 38 seats, the annual subscription is $46,740, with implementation at $6,500 one-time. If you add the 12 seats later, those would prorate through the same June 30 term end.

segments.speaker: Customer
segments.text: That term end matters. Our procurement team wants everything aligned to June 30. Can you make the invoice dated August 1 but payment due net 45?

segments.speaker: Rep
segments.text: Yes, net 45 is fine. I can set the start date as August 1, invoice date August 1, due September 15. Go-live would be August 26 if we get signature by July 24.

segments.speaker: Customer
segments.text: That timeline works. Legal had two comments: they want mutual indemnity language left as-is, and they asked for a 30-day termination right if the uptime SLA is missed twice in a quarter.

segments.speaker: Rep
segments.text: On the indemnity, no issue. On termination for SLA misses, I’ll need to route that through deal desk. Just being transparent, my mornings this week have been getting eaten by clerical stuff — updating pipeline stages, tidying required fields in the database, and assembling internal approval forms — and it cuts directly into the hours I’m supposed to be on buyer calls. I’ll still get this routed today, but I may send the redline late afternoon.

segments.speaker: Customer
segments.text: Okay. If you can send it by 5:00 Eastern, I can get our counsel to review tomorrow. We’re trying to avoid this slipping into August.

segments.speaker: Rep
segments.text: Understood. I’ll send the redline and the quote together. The quote will show 38 seats, $46,740 annual, $6,500 implementation, August 1 start, June 30 end, net 45 payment terms.

segments.speaker: Customer
segments.text: Good. Also please include the purchase order number field blank. AP won’t issue the PO until after legal signs off, but they want the field visible.

segments.speaker: Rep
segments.text: Yep, I’ll leave the PO field blank and visible. I’ll email everything today, and then we can hold 20 minutes Friday at 11:30 to confirm procurement status.
